Classification guard: the single authored edge asserts association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly:true) - it records that phantom pain is a frequent and clinically salient post-amputation phenomenon, documented in a hemipelvectomy/hindquarter series and in a nationwide amputee survey, not that hemipelvectomy caused phantom pain in any individual; individual claims require documented amputation level and date, validated phantom-pain characterization with chronology, and separation of phantom pain from residual-limb pain, neuroma pain, and other pain generators.

Family-scope guard: phantom-limb-pain is owned per-site by the limb-loss identities (six existing site-specific edges), and hemipelvectomy is the most proximal lower-limb hindquarter loss identity, so this edge follows the established per-site pattern rather than duplicating the published amputation-or-loss-of-use container, which owns the generic amputation-to-depression window.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 43 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - hemipelvectomy to phantom-limb-pain (rank 1), ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, and mechanismCategory NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION mirroring the existing per-site limb-loss edges. The proposition rests on the Grimer 2013 hindquarter-amputation series of 157 procedures, which reports that phantom pain was a significant problem in that population and documents the amputation-level and oncologic context, supported by the Diers 2022 nationwide survey of 3,374 unilateral limb amputees as the family-level prevalence and phenomenology anchor. The edge is not raised to causation: the located evidence documents high post-amputation prevalence and clinical salience without prospectively quantifying incident phantom pain attributable to hemipelvectomy specifically, the primary population is oncologic, and phantom phenomena overlap with residual-limb and neuroma pain, so no probability estimate is asserted.

Amputation-family screen recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no depressive-disorder edge - the published amputation-or-loss-of-use container identity already owns the generic amputation-to-depression window (Mckechnie 2014 systematic review of anxiety and depression after traumatic limb amputation), and no hemipelvectomy-specific depressive-disorder prevalence or direction data were located; the Werenski 2026 cohort on patient perspectives, recovery, and satisfaction after hemipelvectomy for pelvic tumors reports functional, psychosocial, and care-burden outcomes rather than depressive-disorder incidence or direction, so it was screened and not cited as a depressive-disorder source (population and zero-record guards); (ii) no unexplained-chronic-pain edge - post-amputation pain is phenotype-explained by the amputation and its phantom and residual-limb mechanisms, and the unexplained-chronic-pain window requires delay and quantification evidence absent here (constitutive and zero-record guards); (iii) no lymphedema edge - lymphedema is a master-resolution target-only-draft identity whose zero-suggestion invariant must be preserved (target-integrity guard); (iv) no heterotopic-ossification, wound-infection, prosthetic-complication, or rehabilitation-limitation edge - no condition-specific directional data were located for this primary (zero-record guard); (v) sibling scope - hip-disarticulation, knee-disarticulation, amputation-of-thumb-fingers-toes, shoulder-disarticulation, and wrist-disarticulation remain unbacklogged sibling identities with their own site windows that this edge does not pre-empt (duplicate-scope guard).

Source-reuse note recorded 2026-09-24: PMID 34583023 already anchors five existing per-site phantom-limb-pain edges in the registry as a human-verified (verified:true, active) source; it is reused here as the family-level prevalence anchor and is therefore carried verified:true in this draft edge, matching the elbow-disarticulation family precedent, while the hemipelvectomy-specific proposition rests on the Grimer hindquarter series (verified:false, pending human review) rather than on the reused survey alone. Deduplication is handled by the registry lockstep: the reuse adds one live use to the existing source entity without adding a new source.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Grimer 2013 series of 157 hindquarter amputations reports that phantom pain was a significant problem in that population, and the Diers 2022 nationwide survey of 3,374 unilateral limb amputees characterizes phantom limb pain prevalence and phenomenology across amputation levels - a reproducible post-amputation association that is not an individual causal nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the located evidence documents high post-amputation prevalence and clinical salience without prospectively quantifying incident phantom pain attributable to hemipelvectomy specifically, the primary hemipelvectomy population is oncologic, and phantom sensation overlaps with residual-limb pain, neuroma pain, and pre-amputation pain, so an individual determination requires documented amputation level and date, validated phantom-pain characterization with chronology, and competing-generator review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Peripheral nerve transection at the hindquarter level with subsequent maladaptive dorsal-horn and cortical sensorimotor reorganization is hypothesized to generate phantom sensation and phantom pain in the absent limb; the located evidence documents that phantom pain is a frequent and clinically significant problem after hindquarter amputation and characterizes its prevalence across amputation levels, while the individual pathway must be established from pain characterization, amputation records, and specialist evaluation.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Pre-amputation pain intensity, residual-limb and neuroma pathology, and prosthetic or rehabilitation factors may modify the individual pain course and must be separated from the phantom-pain proposition.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: a hemipelvectomy/hindquarter series reports phantom pain as a significant problem in that population and a nationwide amputee survey characterizes phantom-limb-pain prevalence across levels, but population prevalence and series reporting do not establish an individual medical nexus without documentation of the amputation and the phantom-pain syndrome, compatible chronology, and competing-cause review, so no at-least-as-likely-as-not probability is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of the hemipelvectomy or hindquarter amputation (level, cause, date); documented phantom limb pain by validated assessment with onset chronology after the amputation; distinction of phantom pain from residual-limb pain, neuroma pain, and pre-amputation pain; assessment of pre-amputation pain, oncologic treatment history, and prosthetic or rehabilitation factors; specialist assessment distinguishing phantom pain from other post-amputation pain generators
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Neuropathic pain from tumor involvement or oncologic treatment
Musculoskeletal or prosthetic-fit pain of the remaining pelvis and spine
